about.title: Sausalito Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Sausalito's collisions often cluster along Bridgeway and the US-101 corridors, especially on Saturday afternoons when weekend traffic and visitor congestion pick up. Marin County's most recent count showed 31 injury collisions and 38 people injured, a reminder that even a small waterfront town sees its share of serious crashes. If you were injured in one of these incidents, the days right after matter: photos of the scene, witness names, and medical records can quietly disappear if no one collects them. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge you anything; we simply connect injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who takes cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. That attorney can help you understand your options, deal with insurance adjusters, and decide what your claim may be worth given California's rules on fault and damages.
commonInjuries: Torn ligaments and soft tissue damage

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Pure Comparative Fault Rule
items.desc: Even if you were partly at fault, you can still recover a share of damages proportional to the other driver's responsibility. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of fault isn't inflated by the insurance company.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. That makes it especially important to have someone document how the injury has actually affected your daily life.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Early evidence preservation and prompt legal guidance can prevent avoidable deadline problems.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.
